docs.text: Happy Year of the Snake! 🐍 The Lake Erie Water Snake - once near the point of extinction before being delisted from the federal Endangered Species List in 2011 - is a #GreatLakes success story about the power of public education and habitat protection #LunarNewYear blog.nature.org/2017/01/23/r...

🐍Eastern massasauga (Sistrurus catenatus). Max size 76 cm (29.9"). Being a species of rattlesnake it is of course venomous. Found in the Great Lakes region of Canada and the US as far south as southern Illinois. Considered Least Concern by the IUCN. 📷by Abhishek Navlakha on Pexels

He was just sunning himself. He's a non-venomous water snake. Mostly these guys are around the Lake Erie Islands to the west. Surprised to see one in the city. I hear their population has grown significantly thanks to a tasty and easy-to-catch invasive fish species, the Asian Goby.
Did another snake survey today and my god I had so much fun! Got a bunch of kisses from some Lake Erie water snakes too :3

After seeing a post online, we had to make a run up to the garden to see the new baby massasauga rattlesnakes! One took up residence in a drainage pipe in the Great Lakes Garden and it gave birth this week! It is cordoned off, but so cool to see so close. #massasaugarattlesnake 🌱🐍
The recovery of the Lake Erie water snake is an awesome story of how outreach can increase support for less-cuddly endangered species blog.nature.org/2017/01/23/r...
Can you see him? Just left of centre. Lake Erie Water Snake - just a young ‘un. Me, Mr. Beagle and a few of the town are out snake hunting - one lad saw 11! 😊

My cousin Faye arrived at my home yesterday by canoe on their 21-day adventure paddling from the St Clair River to Crystal Beach. En route, they spotted a Lake Erie water snake! I remember seeing so many in my youth and sadly thought they were extinct. But Nerodia sipedon insularum is recovering!😍

DH is that way too. When we moved here, he was terrified of the Lake Erie Water Snakes sunning themselves on the rocks at the marina. Now, he’s gotten to the point where he can admire them 😊 Me, I grew up with snakes . No big deal 👍🏼
The Canadian Pacific Grade Snakes Along the Lake Superior Coast. Jackfish, Ontario

Two blue snakes from opposite ends of the US. Both are called racers but not closely related. The Blue Racer is found in the Great Lakes area, and the Speckled Racer is found way down in the southern most parts of Texas.

Well, fuck. I live ten minutes from Lake Erie. Now I want to never visit again. Water snakes scare me because I do not enjoy sensing something moving in the murky depths beneath me. I don't like it when something touches my leg. Eel, snake, seaweed, I don't care, I hate it all.
Water snake exhausted by the pounding northeast winds on Lake Erie.

I live in the Great Lakes region of North America, so I'm less worried about snakes than I am about mosquitoes and the like. I'm also old enough to remember that the bugs used to be way worse than they are now. That actually kinda worries me to be honest.
I’ve seen all the snakes of Lake Michigan. Here in SW Mi.

In the Toronto area for years the massassagua rattler was thought extinct along with its much larger cousin the King. We don’t tell folks but Toronto Island chain has a snake preserve full of them. Boating Lake Huron my wife & took dinghy to shore for BBQ and spotted a King Sunning huge fat female

Freshman year of college my first weekend home I found my sisters used my room as a lounge, they got a corn snake named NAGINI and put him next to my bed. Now I have to worry about snakes in the water? Lake Superior doesn't have water snakes. Why cant Erie be like it's big sister Superior.

We see garters too & black rat snakes. They're impressive but harmless. There are water snakes that swim in Lake Erie like little Nessies too.

The Eastern Massasauga Rattlesnake (Sistrurus catenatus) inhabits the Great Lakes region of North America, spanning from Ontario, Canada, down through the U.S. Midwest.

Ontario has one native species of rattlesnake. The native range used stretch along the southern shores of lake Ontario, and the shores of lake Erie and Huron, all the way up to the northern shore of Georgian Bay. Now it's limited to populations in the Bruce Peninsula, Wainfleet, and Windsor area.
The eastern massasauga rattlesnake is native to the lower peninsula of Michigan and several other Great Lakes states.
